topic_tag: a garden scene in a stage comedy
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Most critics now describe the garden scene as the play's ______.

worlds.passage: Midway through a three-act comedy first staged in 1926, about a brother and sister quarreling over their late father's house, comes a short scene set in a moonlit garden. The playwright wrote it during rehearsals, when the designer needed four minutes to change the scenery behind a drop curtain. In it the servants dance and no one speaks; when the action resumes, the brother picks up his accusation mid-sentence, and audiences have always applauded the dance as loudly as anything in the play. Most critics now describe the garden scene as the play's ______.
worlds.explanation: A wordless dance covering a scene change, after which the brother resumes mid-sentence, is the play's "interlude." "Kernel" fails because it was written during rehearsals; "letdown" fails because audiences applaud it as loudly as anything; "hinge" fails because the quarrel resumes exactly where it stopped.

kernel.why: a late addition is not the core the play grew from

letdown.why: a scene audiences love is not a disappointment

hinge.why: nothing changes, so nothing turns on it

worlds.passage: Midway through a three-act comedy first staged in 1926, about a brother and sister quarreling over their late father's house, comes a short scene set in a moonlit garden. The playwright's notebooks show it written ten years before anything else in the play, as a sketch of two children locked out of a garden, and every later scene borrows from it: the lost key, the father's voice offstage, the gate itself. In it the quarrel runs on as bitterly as before; the house is settled only in the final act, and revivals keep the garden whatever else they cut. Most critics now describe the garden scene as the play's ______.
worlds.explanation: Written a decade before the rest, with every later scene borrowing its images, the garden scene is the core the play grew from: its "kernel." "Interlude" fails because the quarrel runs on in it; "letdown" fails because revivals keep it whatever else they cut; "hinge" fails because the house is settled only in the final act.

interlude.quote: the quarrel runs on as bitterly
interlude.why: it is part of the action, not a break from it

letdown.why: a scene always kept is not a disappointment

hinge.quote: settled only in the final act

worlds.passage: Midway through a three-act comedy first staged in 1926, about a brother and sister quarreling over their late father's house, comes a short scene set in a moonlit garden. The playwright wrote it during rehearsals, and in it brother and sister go on quarreling, chiefly by repeating speeches from the first act almost word for word. The house is settled only in the final act; revivals routinely cut the garden, and the playwright himself told an interviewer it was the night he should have gone to bed early. Most critics now describe the garden scene as the play's ______.
worlds.explanation: Recycled speeches, routine cuts in revivals, and the playwright's own regret make the scene the play's "letdown." "Interlude" fails because the quarrel goes on in it; "kernel" fails because it was written during rehearsals; "hinge" fails because the house is settled only in the final act.

interlude.why: it continues the action rather than pausing it

kernel.why: a late addition is not the seed of the play

hinge.quote: settled only in the final act

worlds.passage: Midway through a three-act comedy first staged in 1926, about a brother and sister quarreling over their late father's house, comes a short scene set in a moonlit garden. The playwright wrote it during rehearsals, and in it the quarrel goes on until the brother, half-drunk under the moon, lets slip that he forged their father's will. From the next scene on, the sister holds the house and he is begging for a room in it, and revivals keep the garden whatever else they cut. Most critics now describe the garden scene as the play's ______.
worlds.explanation: After the brother lets slip the forgery here, the sister holds the house and he begs for a room, so the scene is the play's "hinge." "Interlude" fails because the quarrel goes on in it; "kernel" fails because it was written during rehearsals, not the seed of the play; "letdown" fails because revivals keep it whatever else they cut.

interlude.why: it is central action, not a break

kernel.why: a late addition is not the core the play grew from

letdown.why: a scene always kept is not a disappointment
